A.title: Six donors followed across three visits
A.poster_caption: RP1-14 comprises six donors with CD4 and CD8 repertoires at each of three visits, spanning 14.95–24.86 years. The frozen reuse dictionary covers 25,513,582 qualified reads, 508,972 distinct nucleotide-CDR3/V/J identities and 4,958 receptor functional units (RFUs).
A.manuscript_legend: RP1-14 study design and coverage. Each donor contributes three chronological visits and both CD4 and CD8 repertoires, giving 36 samples over 14.95–24.86 years. Filled circles denote CD4 and open squares denote CD8 throughout the figure set. The timeline uses the frozen elapsed-year metadata, not source-filename order. Depth bars sum all source reads and qualified reads across the three visits separately for each donor and compartment; the full per-sample depths and fractions are supplied in A_samples.tsv. The summary counts are 70,960,689 source reads, 25,513,582 qualified reads, 508,972 distinct qualified nucleotide-CDR3/V/J identities (not the sum of per-sample richness), and 4,958 qualified RFUs. Qualified reads use the fixed historical assignment dictionary applied to full productive counts and the unchanged score threshold of 0.6. Sequencing reads are not cell or template counts, and coverage remains conditional on the recoverable assignment universe.
A.take_home: A complete longitudinal design supports paired comparisons within six donors.
A.recommended_use: Poster overview and methods-paper main figure.

B.title: Change depends on representation
B.poster_caption: Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J) is higher than RFU TV in both compartments; lines connect the same donor. Lower group-level total variation (TV) partly reflects aggregation and does not establish preserved antigen function.
B.manuscript_legend: Earliest-to-latest total variation (TV) for the six paired donors, shown separately for CD4 and CD8 on identical 0–1 scales. The manuscript version includes Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J), RFU TV, TRBV TV and V/J TV; the poster version focuses on receptor and RFU TV. Thin lines connect representations for one donor, and thick black bars show equal-donor medians. All representations use the same threshold-qualified receptor universe and sequencing-read weights. TRBV denotes the recorded T-cell receptor beta variable-call category; V/J denotes the recorded joint variable/joining-call category, including frozen family-only or unresolved labels. Smaller distances at coarser granularity are not evidence of superior functional stability. TV is zero for identical normalized distributions and one for disjoint distributions; receptor functional units (RFUs) are group labels, not measured antigen functions.
B.take_home: Aggregation lowers apparent change; the magnitude depends on the representation.
B.recommended_use: Methods-paper main figure; optional poster alternative to the control panel.

C.title: Matched controls show similar cancellation
C.poster_caption: Aggregation cancellation is receptor total variation (TV) minus receptor functional unit (RFU) TV. Similar cancellation under matched random-grouping controls shows that this effect is not uniquely RFU-specific.
C.manuscript_legend: TV denotes total variation and RFU denotes receptor functional unit. Donor-level aggregation cancellation for earliest-to-latest read-weighted comparisons: Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J) minus RFU TV. Filled circles (CD4) and open squares (CD8) show observed RFU cancellation; open diamonds show each donor's median across 30 frozen matched maps, and horizontal ranges are their 2.5th–97.5th percentiles using linear interpolation. Observed and control rows are slightly displaced vertically only for visibility. The frozen control permutes RFU labels among pooled eligible receptor identities within recorded V-call, J-call and five-amino-acid CDR3-length-bin strata, retaining the label counts within strata; each map is fixed across visits. Matched-map cancellation uses the same receptor TV minus the matched-group TV. Each compartment contains the same six donors; maps are technical control replicates, not independent donors, confidence intervals or calibrated null tests. Similar cancellation supports an aggregation contribution and does not demonstrate special preservation of antigen function by RFUs. Recorded family-only and unresolved calls constrain the specificity of feature matching.
C.take_home: Similar cancellation under matched controls is not uniquely RFU-specific.
C.recommended_use: Highest-priority poster and methods-paper main panel.

D.title: Persistent RFUs can hide receptor turnover
D.poster_caption: Among RFUs detected at five or more qualified reads in both endpoint visits, median fractions without a shared observed receptor are 41.4% in CD4 and 59.8% in CD8. Observed RFU persistence does not establish preserved antigen function.
D.manuscript_legend: Observed receptor functional unit (RFU) persistence and constituent-receptor overlap in the frozen earliest-to-latest results. An RFU is persistent when it has at least five qualified reads at each endpoint visit. The manuscript panel shows persistent RFUs divided by the union detected at either endpoint and, separately, persistent RFUs with no shared observed nucleotide-CDR3/V/J receptor divided by all persistent RFUs. Lines link the same donor's CD4 and CD8 measurements; bars are equal-donor medians, not RFU-pooled fractions. The corresponding median fractions without shared observed receptors are 0.4140 and 0.5983. Counts and both denominators are retained in D_donors.tsv. The poster and manuscript assembly emphasize the latter fraction, with a programmatic explanatory schematic of one hypothetical RFU containing receptors a/b early and c/d late. Those arbitrary letters are not biological sequences or measured frequencies. Nondetection does not establish biological absence; apparent group persistence cannot establish preserved antigen function.
D.take_home: The same observed RFU need not contain the same observed receptors.
D.recommended_use: High-priority poster and methods-paper main panel.

E.title: Sampling and weighting change the estimate
E.poster_caption: Median RFU TV changes under unique-receptor weighting and the frozen 500-read-per-visit sensitivity. These are measurement boundaries: read subsamples do not measure donor uncertainty or cell/template sampling.
E.manuscript_legend: RFU denotes receptor functional unit and TV denotes total variation. Frozen sensitivity comparisons for the same earliest-to-latest donor pairs and threshold-qualified receptor universe. Observed sequencing-read weights, one count per unique observed nucleotide-CDR3/V/J identity per visit, and 500 observed reads sampled without replacement per endpoint are displayed. Each 500-read point is the within-donor median of the existing 50 subsamples; manuscript whiskers show the corresponding 2.5th–97.5th percentiles (linear interpolation). The manuscript panel includes RFU TV and aggregation cancellation separately for CD4 and CD8, retaining the paired donor structure. The compact poster panel shows individual donor values with heavier lines joining equal-donor medians; its 500-read summary is the median of within-donor medians, not a pool of 300 resamples. All draws are reused, with no new sampling or fitted endpoints. Sampling is conditional on observed sequencing reads and historical assignment coverage, not actual cells/templates; the ranges are not donor confidence intervals. No additional matched-depth result is implied beyond the frozen common 500-read sensitivity.
E.take_home: Interpret stability estimates together with their depth and weighting choices.

F.title: Alignment repaired; assignments verified
F.poster_caption: The repair preserves all 359,530 RFU/score-vector entries and removes all 41,572 repeated-amino-acid RFU-assignment conflicts. Frozen stratified parity matches 1,600/1,600 labels and threshold decisions, including 485 near-threshold receptors.
F.manuscript_legend: RFU denotes receptor functional unit. Supplementary summary of the completed RP1-14 row-alignment repair audit. All 359,530 saved RFU/score-vector entries are unchanged; 330,433 amino-acid row labels were repaired and 29,097 retained. Repeated-amino-acid conflict groups decrease from 41,572 to zero for RFU assignments and from 41,581 to zero for scores. The already completed stratified assay agrees on all 1,600 RFU labels and all 1,600 threshold decisions, including 485 historical scores in [0.59, 0.61). The maximum absolute score discrepancy is 1.0547118733938987e-15, below the frozen 1e-12 tolerance. Stratification rows partition the same assay in different ways and must not be summed across factors. These checks support the bounded alignment repair; they do not recreate an unavailable historical invocation manifest or prove parity for unassayed receptors. No repair or reference assignment was rerun to create this figure.
F.take_home: The verified repair changes row labels while preserving saved assignments and scores.
F.recommended_use: Manuscript supplementary figure and optional poster/Q&A backup.

poster_block.title: RP1-14: aggregation can mask receptor turnover
poster_block.poster_caption: Reusable RP1-14 figure block: A, design and coverage; C, observed and matched-control cancellation; D, persistent groups with changing observed receptors; E, depth and weighting boundaries. The same six donors contribute both compartments.
poster_block.manuscript_legend: Poster assembly of reusable panels A, C, D and E, drawn directly from their source tables with the same panel functions. Letters retain the reusable figure identifiers. The 30-by-20-inch block is intended for placement near its native size on an A0 poster; it is a figure block rather than a complete poster. RFU means receptor functional unit and TV means total variation. All scientific definitions, donors and uncertainty descriptions are those in the individual panel legends.
poster_block.take_home: Persistent aggregate profiles can coexist with constituent turnover and sampling sensitivity.
poster_block.recommended_use: APBC 2026 poster figure block, at 762 × 508 mm.

manuscript_main.title: RP1-14 longitudinal benchmark
manuscript_main.poster_caption: Manuscript assembly of A–D with explicit representation and matched-control comparisons. All panels reuse the frozen RP1-14 endpoints.
manuscript_main.manuscript_legend: RP1-14 longitudinal benchmark, assembled from reusable panels A–D. A, six donors, three visits and complete CD4/CD8 coverage, donor/compartment read depths summed across visits, and qualified-universe totals. B, paired earliest-to-latest Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J), RFU TV, TRBV TV and V/J TV, separately for CD4 and CD8; bars show medians across six donors. C, observed aggregation cancellation and medians with 2.5th–97.5th percentile ranges from 30 fixed feature/size-matched maps; these are technical ranges, not donor confidence intervals. D, persistent RFUs with no shared observed receptor divided by all persistent RFUs, with a clearly labeled hypothetical schematic. Persistence requires at least five qualified reads in both endpoint visits; lines pair the same donor across compartments. RFU denotes receptor functional unit and TV denotes total variation. Read subsampling/weighting sensitivity (E) and repair QC (F) remain separate supplementary panels. The original six-panel rp1_14_longitudinal figure is preserved unchanged, including its within/between-donor similarity and paired-compartment views. This new assembly changes presentation, not endpoints or conclusions. Aggregation contributes to lower group-level TV, matched controls show similar cancellation, and persistence does not demonstrate preserved antigen function.
manuscript_main.take_home: Measure receptor change, aggregation and observed persistence together.
manuscript_main.recommended_use: Refined methods-paper main-figure draft; original six-panel figure remains available.
